clusters.unsourced_summary: The clinical motivation is asserted bare on the manuscript pages and sourced only in the outward documents: the 179 gold-fiducial placements over 38 months (naming-vertebrae-without-an-anchor-3dfzmh, naming-vertebrae-without-ct-hjy4vc, vertebral-levels-without-ct-a4rydj), half of surveyed surgeons having operated at the wrong level (hjy4vc, a4rydj, counting-levels-under-fluoroscopy, with the specialty changing between pages), 81% of events being a count gone wrong (counting-levels-under-fluoroscopy), 15 of 100 consecutive discectomies (hjy4vc, a4rydj), and 'a surgeon counts from whatever landmark is visible' (3dfzmh, the aidas proposal); the aidas proposal and level-counting-visual-abstract give Siminski 2023, Mody 2008, Furuya 2026 and Goodkin 2004, but the pages that will become the paper do not. Literature benchmarks are quoted without citation where they set the bar: 'best published registration-free naming is 73.3%' and 'published class-agnostic C-arm detection reaches 0.96–0.98' and the '28-point sim-to-real tax' (counting-from-the-sacrum), 'the best whole-spine identification in the literature is 96.5%, on MRI' (overnight-the-honest-99-kantj8), 69.6%/97.6% attributed only to 'published literature' (hjy4vc), and the 88.3% Huang figure that registration-free-level-id-feasibility-uramo1 says failed verification (hjy4vc, a4rydj, fluorocap-reality-check-czudvb). Prevalence priors are unsourced where used: L6 in roughly 2% of people (counting-against-two-anchors-qkktgu), Castellvi I as two-thirds or 68% of LSTV (overnight-99, research-directions), 'C1 is excluded from these datasets' (vertebral-count-anomaly-rule). Novelty is claimed by unrecorded searches: no published frame-chaining method (3dfzmh), no AP-to-lateral synthesis and 'lateral naming is already at the ceiling' (any-view-spine-plan), no lumbosacral 3-D classifier (research-directions), no evidence that navigation reduces wrong-level surgery (visual abstract, aidas). Operational figures shown to a surgeon and a funder are marked unverified by their own pages: cadaver work needing no IRB and fifteen business days (counting-levels-under-fluoroscopy, aidas), navigation capital of $1–2.5M (visual abstract), 'costs milliseconds' (hjy4vc), 'about 3% in ordinary use' (a4rydj), 'surgeons centre the field the same way' (or-readiness-ledger), 'the OR always has both AP and lateral views' (lift-before-label-jzjq8t), 'the count from the sacrum is undetermined in a limited field' (schwingnet-figures-xyz6kr).
clusters.stale_summary: Every member carries lines that have moved by 2026-10-22. The September-17/18 manuscript pages (naming-vertebrae-without-an-anchor-3dfzmh, naming-vertebrae-without-ct-hjy4vc, vertebral-levels-without-ct-a4rydj) say jobs 40321409 and 40321779 are running, 'when they land they replace this table', a 376-patient transitional cross-validation is running, and 'a verified search finished today'; the handoff of 2026-10-08 later rules the allspine v2, v6, v7, anchor_drr and vindrps numbers 'record only' and says nothing after 2026-09-27 changed the banks or models. The September-22 pages (counting-from-the-sacrum, or-readiness-ledger, both figures pages) list a fleet detector 'training now', the CTSpinoPelvic1K id-is-a-person audit running (answered 2026-10-08 as 301 of 801 persons on both sides), jobs 40411495/40411934 and device fits running, a sampler 'not adopted' pending A/B, the composite 'not yet restacked' at 20:12 and Figures 4 and 6 failed at 22:50. The undated design pages (counting-against-two-anchors-qkktgu: arms not run; vertebra-detector-field-report-1jljc6: CSXA behind a browser session, BUU 77 of 7,200 files, level head not started) describe states the ladder and handoff have passed. The outward documents are dated: the aidas proposal was due 2026-10-16 with '[to confirm]' placeholders and refiners 'being measured as arms'; counting-levels-under-fluoroscopy says 'start this week' and 'the manuscript in preparation'; the handoff records the disclosure submitted 2026-09-25 with the provisional filing not recorded, the CNS talk 31 Oct–4 Nov and paper 1 held for tech transfer. candidates.topic: Number of lumbar-rib cases in CTSpinoPelvic1K (802 records)
candidates.statement_a: Sixteen lumbar-rib examples in the corpus
candidates.quote_a: The model never memorises sixteen lumbar-rib examples in order to recognise one. It learns to count from the sacrum, and to count from the ribs, with ~800 cases of each.
candidates.statement_b: Thirteen cases carry a rib on a lumbar body (and the reader-labelled lumbar-rib set has fourteen members)
candidates.quote_b: The 13 cases carrying a rib on a lumbar body cluster at four, as they must. ... 0008 — labelled SACRALIZATION , the only reader disagreement of the fourteen
candidates.why_it_matters: The lumbar-rib positives are the scarce class the two-anchor design is built to avoid memorising; a planner sizing a stump-rib or lumbar-rib recall test gets 13, 14 or 16 depending on the page, with no statement of which label release or rule each count comes from.

candidates.topic: Whether the CTSpinoPelvic1K label volume ever carries a sixth lumbar vertebra
candidates.statement_a: The label volume assigns L1 to L5 plus a sacrum regardless of the true anatomy
candidates.quote_a: The count is derived from labelled vertebrae, and the label volume assigns L1–L5 plus a sacrum regardless of the true anatomy.
candidates.statement_b: An L6 label exists and is nearly definitional of LSTV (d 4.7); the state-of-the-literature page counts 18 L6 by release label and the decisions page about 22 of 802 cases carrying an L6
candidates.quote_b: | has_l6_label | | 4.7 | | A sixth lumbar label is nearly definitional |
candidates.why_it_matters: If labels always stop at L5 the count can never read six and L6 Dice must be undefined, not zero; if 18 to 22 records carry L6, the audit's explanation of the count's failure is incomplete. A planner chooses between repairing the labels and repairing the count on this point.

candidates.topic: Why sacral foramina fail as an anchor on CTSpinoPelvic1K
candidates.statement_a: The per-side foramina count in normal-labelled cases has mode three (211, 324, 163, 49 at 2 to 5) and overlaps the variants; the measurement is dominated by field of view, many sacra being truncated inferiorly
candidates.quote_a: Counting foramina per side across 802 records gives, for cases labelled normal : 2 in 211 cases, 3 in 324, 4 in 163, 5 in 49. The mode is three, not four , and the distribution overlaps the labelled sacralisations and lumbarisations completely. The measurement is dominated by field of view — many sacra are truncated inferiorly in an abdominal CT.
candidates.statement_b: The detector does not deliver the anatomy: 3 left and 7 right on one symmetric sacrum, small canals close in a bone mask and morphological closing invents others; counts are detector output that undercount true anatomy
candidates.quote_b: The detector does not deliver it. On one symmetric sacrum it returned 3 left and 7 right. Small canals close in a bone mask and morphological closing invents others. ... foramina counts are detector output and undercount true anatomy.
candidates.why_it_matters: Both rule the anchor out, but one blames the scans (unfixable) and the other the detector (fixable); a planner reading only the first would not try a better foramina detector, and one reading only the second might.

candidates.statement_b: Stated as the intended measure's rule, no citation
candidates.quote_b: Intended as the measure that settles sacralization without trusting any vertebra label — four pairs normal, five means the sacrum absorbed L5.
candidates.why_it_matters: Both pages test the detector against this rule and find the corpus's mode is three; without a source a planner cannot tell whether three reflects truncation, the detector, or a wrong textbook rule.

candidates.topic: The ilium's auricular surface and the sacroiliac articulation are unchanged by lumbosacral fusion and can anchor sacralisation

candidates.statement_b: Ilium contact with the L5 transverse process is sacralization, Castellvi II to IV by definition; the sacroiliac height is tight in normal anatomy and shifted by about a segment in transitional cases, no source
candidates.quote_b: If it does, that is sacralization — Castellvi II–IV by definition. ... Height of the sacroiliac articulation against the labelled S1 endplate. One scalar per case: tight in normal anatomy, shifted by about a segment in transitional.
candidates.why_it_matters: The second anchor both designs rest on is an anatomical premise asserted in both and measured in neither; the border page's Castellvi span and gap proxies came out flat (d under 0.2), which is the nearest measurement and does not support it.

clusters.unsourced_summary: The cluster's anchoring anatomy is asserted rather than cited. Counting Against Two Anchors and Spinal Border Variants both state the textbook rule that four pairs of sacral foramina are normal and five mean an absorbed lumbar segment, with no reference, and both then find the corpus's mode is three. Counting Against Two Anchors states that the ilium's auricular surface is not relinquished when a lumbar segment fuses above it, and the Rib Anchor Audit states that ilium contact with the L5 transverse process is sacralization by definition and that sacroiliac height is tight in normal anatomy and shifted by about a segment in transitional cases; neither measures it, and the nearest measurement (the border page's Castellvi span and gap proxies) is flat. Counting Against Two Anchors gives the L6 prevalence as roughly 2% and the lowest-lumbar-is-L5 prior as right 97% of the time without a source, calls the name-prediction defect 'the documented failure mode' without saying where, and says the CNN-over-Transformer finding came from organ segmentation without a citation. The Rib Anchor Audit asserts that thoracic bodies sit about 20 mm apart, that 29% is above and 1.9% is a plausible rate of rib asymmetry, and that counting from C2 on whole-spine imaging is the only definitive method and the reason LSTV is chronically mislabelled (the feasibility page cites Liebrand 2026 and Nakagawa 2017 for related statements, so this one is sourced only indirectly). Overnight: The Honest 99% and Research directions both put Castellvi type I at about two thirds or 68% of LSTV with no citation at the statement, and Overnight: The Honest 99% and State of the literature both quote the VerSe rare-class precedent (15 or 28 L6 training cases sufficing, T13 found by the counting prior) without naming the paper. OpenSpine Board and Spine Program Decisions share, unsourced, the sentence that the published LSTV state of the art is AUC 0.84 at 62.3% prevalence and the reading that BUU's 4.0% is a population rate; the feasibility page is the only member that names the study (Kwak 2025). Overnight: The Honest 99% says one published model attends to the twelfth rib and counts down from it, unnamed. Across the cluster, every variant count on CTSpinoPelvic1K (lumbar ribs 10, 13, 14, 16 or 25; L6 13, 16, 18, 22 or 29; four lumbar 7, 9 or 13; Castellvi 31, 33 or 34) is given as a fact of the corpus with no statement of which label release or counting rule produced it, so an experiment planner would take whichever page they read as established.
clusters.stale_summary: All three primary members are undated and carry status that has moved. Rib Anchor Audit says v5 exists only as a local tree at data/v5_final with nothing pushed to HuggingFace, 107 of 113 spine cases finalized, and its two sacral-boundary tests 'next' and uncomputed; Research directions (8 Oct 2026) has the label tree at v11 with v10 as the public mirror and the Handoff (8 Oct) has the dataset released on Zenodo and Hugging Face. Spinal Border Variants measures 'from data/v5_final' and lists seven cases that 'need a person' (0008, 0389, 0720, 0344, 0179, 0412, 1153) with no record of their resolution. Counting Against Two Anchors says the rib-bearing head is 'already built', the staged pipeline is the comparator 'that already exists', its five arms are to be run with arms 1 and 2 as the result, and its counts are 'measured on the released labels'; by 8 Oct the design is CT-7, ranked 14th with nothing run on the grid, and seven L6 records of the release are out of every truth pool pending re-read. Among the secondaries: LSTV Verification Bench is dated 15 September 2026, 'PubMed Central pass one', with counters at 0 of 0, and Overnight: The Honest 99% (16 Sep) lists the 585-figure bench and a 179-panel bench as waiting for the owner, while Research directions records FluoroCap dropped by directive with no 200-panel test set. FluoroCap Overnight Report (15 Sep) says nothing has taught the model a T13 and the corpus has no real T13 or L6 panel; the next day's table has 254 T13 and 338 L6 panels and the naming page (17 Sep) brings 78 T13 and 114 L6 vertebrae into bank v7. OpenSpine Board (11 Sep) marks BUU's LSTV truth 'unused' and lists purging the IRB files as waiting on the owner; Spine Program Decisions records the purge done and says a rare-class fold count is 'running now' and L6 Dice 0.00 is 'investigating', which Research directions closes as measured (Dice 0.000 with twelvefold duplication). Registration-Free Level ID Feasibility (15 Sep) finds no public intraoperative fluoroscopy set with level labels and says 'nothing is stale' as of that date; State of the literature (8 Oct) holds one (C-ArmLSpine) with no human transitional read, and Research directions and the Handoff both say the verified real-frame transitional test count is zero 'today' against 35 needed, with every data request drafted and none sent, 33 Castellvi grades against 71 to 142 expected, and the CNS meeting of 31 Oct to 4 Nov 2026 ahead. Research directions also notes the VerSe L6 count disagrees across files (85, 47, 50 or 87) and that the 2026-09-17 refutation of pretrain-then-fine-tune was never re-run on a clean bank.
clusters.notes: Worked from the fourteen records in full and from the plain text of the three primaries, the honest-99 anomaly table, the naming page's co-occurrence paragraphs and the research-directions project rows; quotes from the other secondaries are the records' own. The decisive find is in the naming page's supplementary text (not in its record): on CTSpinoPelvic1K the co-occurrence both-cell was two (OR 4.00 [1.00, 16.03]) against the border page's 44 (OR 19.6) on the same 802 scans, which the naming page attributes to the abdominopelvic field not reaching the upper ribs; the two pages define a thoracolumbar variant differently (rib-12 length ratio versus label-voxel flags). The border page's '35 at four and 26 at six' labelled LSTV cases exceed its own 33 non-normal labels, and research-directions' CT-7 gate gives yet a third cell layout; I read the border page's 35 and 26 as all cases at those counts despite its wording. The audit's two lumbar-rib numbers (14 by strict incidence, 25 ribs on a lumbar vertebra) are in one artifact; I paired them with research-directions' 10 so the entry has two artifacts. The order between the undated border page and the naming page (17 Sep) is unknown, so 19.6 versus 3.61 is reported as a contradiction, not a supersession; the naming page's 'smaller than first tabulated' refers to its own all-rows 4.30. Dates: Research directions, State of the literature and the Handoff are all 8 Oct 2026 from the second account and repeat each other; where they agree they are one source. No e-mail, phone or address appears in the records; the grid login the board's header carries is not reproduced. The clustering's canonical set is reasonable, but its empty superseded list misses that the border page carries the audit's rib numbering forward (109 to 19) and that the decisions page supersedes the board.

canonical_check.why: The handoff (3 Sep) records the film corpora as 77 BUU files, 0 CSXA images and IEEE, AASCE and BUU behind forms; the manifest (8 Oct) records the same corpora on disk at full size (CSXA 4,963 films; BUU 3,600 patients, 7,200 films; NHANES 17,073 and 543; VinDr 10,466; AASCE 609; Mendeley 714; IEEE 236; Spinal-AI 20,000), and the any-view plan says in its own words that the 3 Sep handoff had 77 BUU files while it reports BUU as held with 3,600 people. The manifest does not cite the handoff and does not carry its rules (the 208 Honduran films as the only cross-site test set, IEEE never for training, patient-disjoint splits, VinDr as restricted rather than credentialed), and the registry later excludes Mendeley outright, so the later page supersedes the holdings but not the lineage decisions; those survive only on the handoff, the board and the decisions page.

clusters.unsourced_summary: The September pages (the X-ray handoff and the vertebra-detector field report) assert that CSXA is the largest annotated lateral set in existence, that CM Spine is the only public intraoperative source, and that Google Drive caps folder downloads at about 50 files, none with a survey or a citation; the board and the decisions page, which copy each other, assert that no published work uses DRRs to supply level identity to a 2D model, that the published state of the art on radiographs is AUC 0.84 at 62.3 % prevalence without naming the study, and that 4.0 % is the population LSTV rate, which the protocol draft puts at 15.3 % and research directions at 9 to 18 %. The 8 October trio (the handoff, the literature-state and research directions) share the statements that every planning value assumed 95 to 99 % with no measurement behind it, that 97.6 % cannot be exceeded at any reachable n, and that no radiologist has read any acquired CT, with the power figures 35, 22 and 19 and the accuracy pair 97.4 % and 74.8 % repeated without run ids or the calculation. The manifest, the registry and the FluoroCap card repeat that no patient was imaged for FluoroCap as the ethics basis with no determination cited. The atlas calls SX-Stitch the only published collection of overlapping intraoperative C-arm frames while the registry calls the Bern runs the only overlapping travelling frames found and the C-ArmLSpine sweeps the only confirmed consecutive sequences with a paired volume. Research directions states that Castellvi type I is 68 % of all LSTV with no reference. Licence statements for BUU (an EULA forbidding redistribution, on the manifest and research directions) stand beside the registry's own line that the licence is unread by the owner.
clusters.stale_summary: Every primary page is dated and overtaken: the X-ray handoff's grid state was verified 3 September 2026 (77 BUU files, no CSXA, IEEE behind a subscription, PhysioNet DUA 1.5.0, CSXA V3.0); the manifest is as of 7 October with batch B00 cut over and its finalize pending, B13 awaiting the owner's decision, the home walk still running, live routes untested and six licence conflicts (CTPelvic1K, VerSe, DeepFluoro, Geneva hip, Ljubljana, SpineSAC) marked unknown; the literature-state of 8 October says it is being cross-referenced and that no drafted request is recorded as sent; the atlas is as of 17 October with every request line reading Sent: not recorded and the Radiopaedia fee unconfirmed that day; the registry was rendered 20 October with its sample-level counts empty until a grid job runs, case39 with no export yet, LUMOS never fetched, RSNA 2022 never unpacked, ten VerSe series never downloaded, BUU's licence unread, VinDr's own determination pending, Balgrist and SX-Stitch requests drafted and never sent, and no gated CT agreement signed. The grid pipeline of 21 October then records 26 requests sent and 5 granted, a signed and paid Radiopaedia licence awaiting countersignature, VinDr-PCXR access granted on 21 October, an RSNA RATIC download link that expires 2026-10-28 02:38 UTC, 15 recipes still marked to confirm, no shard built and no job run, on a schedule running 23 October to 2 November with the provisional filing on 30 October and the CNS talk on 2 November. The secondary pages carry their own dates: the FluoroCap card's manifest was generated 2026-09-14 with reader labels pending and version 0.3 in progress; the board is dated 11 September with IRB files still public (the decisions page records the purge done); the lab recipe says the public mirror is still v10 on 2026-09-27; the 8 October handoff says the provisional filing is not recorded and the migration in progress; research directions says nothing ran on the grid and 33 were graded today; the any-view plan says the census job goes to the grid next and the IPCAI 2025 set is not yet held; the retrospective protocol is Date Submitted: Draft with an AIDaS deadline of 16 October 2026 already past and a target of January 2027; the eProtocol draft is dated 15 September with its 40,000-study cohort unconfirmed; and the COBRA embargoed cases are released on 2032-03-01.
clusters.notes: The plain-text extracts of the registry and the atlas truncate their embedded arrays after the first entry, so the registry's 60 records were read from the page's own JSON (const DATA in /home/user/SchwingNet/artifacts/schwingnet-data-registry/index.html) and the atlas's 217 entries from window.ATLAS in /home/user/SchwingNet/artifacts/fluoroscopy-data-atlas/index.html, extracted with a script run under python3 -I into /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/1b2f17bd-1fd4-5865-b98a-4797cc8ea3ad/scratchpad/helper/cluster_ds/registry.json and atlas.json; the quoted registry and atlas lines were verified there, the other artifacts' quotes come from their inventory records. The atlas entries confirmed the 150 Elekta exports, the SX-Stitch 'only published collection' line, DysphagiaBank at 87 files and 19 GB held, SpineSAC at 5,492 files with five or six C-arms, and the Bournemouth lumbar set as the only confirmed lumbar cine (a request source, so not in conflict with the atlas's 'found nowhere public' for lateral lumbar flexion-extension). Secondary pages dated 11 to 27 September (the board, decisions, lab recipe, field report, X-ray handoff, FluoroCap card, protocol drafts) are earlier than every primary page and most of their disagreements with the October pages are superseded holdings rather than live contradictions; they are listed where the later page does not say it replaces them. No e-mail address, phone number or home address was reproduced; people are named by role (the owner, the labellers, the corresponding authors, one neurosurgeon).

clusters.cluster: FluoroCap: the corpus, its pipeline and its audits

candidates.topic: Figure-mate region agreement with constraint decoding versus the level model alone (same corpus, same date, 2026-09-14)
candidates.statement_a: The card's evaluation table gives 88% figure-mate region agreement for the decoder and 52% for the model alone, with no pair count.
candidates.quote_a: figure mates agreeing on region (decoder) | 88% | panels of the same figure with the same caption levels; 52% for the model alone (partly induced by the shared caption)
candidates.statement_b: The audit of the same day gives 91.5% for the decoder on 519 pairs and 52.1% for the model alone on 468 pairs.
candidates.quote_b: Constraint decoding lifts caption-free region agreement from 52.1% to 91.5% ... 519 pairs for the decoder, 468 for the model run alone.
candidates.why_it_matters: The decoder's headline number is either 88% or 91.5% for the same quantity on the same date; a planner citing one page misquotes the other, and only the audit says how many pairs were counted.

candidates.topic: What the panels without a vertebra box are: detector misses or non-radiographs
candidates.statement_a: The audit reads the 71% of known panels without a box as mostly detector misses, because the modality classifier scores 93% on a held-out set.
candidates.quote_a: Only 29% of known panels produced a vertebra box . The modality classifier scores 93% on a held-out set of 2,143 panels, so a large share of the missing 71% is detector miss rather than a panel that is not a radiograph.
candidates.statement_b: The reality check scores nearly half the corpus as not an x-ray at all, and 35% of the level-labelled panels as not spine radiographs.
candidates.quote_b: 8,843 (49%) score as not an x-ray at all. In the released manifest of 17,486 rows, 9,036 sit below the 0.3 floor, 4,218 pass the default inclusion rules, and human_qc_status reads pending on every row. Of the 2,071 decoded panels that carry level labels, 732 (35%) are
candidates.why_it_matters: The two readings point to opposite fixes: detector recall work under the audit, corpus filtering under the reality check; a planner who read only the audit would retrain the detector on a corpus that is half non-radiographs.

candidates.topic: The 2,143-panel held-out set behind the 93% modality score: FluoroCap panels or film-manifest classes
candidates.statement_a: The audit presents the 93% modality score as measured on 2,143 held-out panels and applies it to FluoroCap's missing 71%.
candidates.quote_a: The modality classifier scores 93% on a held-out set of 2,143 panels, so a large share of the missing 71% is detector miss rather than a panel that is not a radiograph.
candidates.statement_b: The reality check says the 2,143 / 800 held-out set is film-manifest classes, not FluoroCap panels, and that modality is unknown for 7,642 of 17,486 manifest rows.
candidates.quote_b: 93.1% modality head / 99.5% view head | | 2,143 / 800 held-out | | film-manifest classes | | not FluoroCap panels; modality is 'unknown' for 7,642 of 17,486 manifest rows
candidates.why_it_matters: The audit's inference about FluoroCap rests on a score measured on a different population; a planner would trust the modality filter on mined figures when it was never tested on them.

candidates.topic: Caption-held-out accuracy of the level model alone, and containment of its level set
candidates.statement_a: The audit (2026-09-14): the level model alone is right 38.3% of the time with the caption held back; containment 56.8% on n = 389.
candidates.quote_a: The level model alone is right 38.3% of the time on panels where the caption was held back. ... 56.8% caption-held-out containment, n = 389
candidates.statement_b: The reality check (2026-09-15): 37.9% on 169 panels; 57.1% containment, Jaccard 0.341, on 380 caption-free panels that are not a random hold-out.
candidates.quote_b: the level model alone is the weakest term in the decoder on real panels (37.9% on 169) ... 57.1% containment, Jaccard 0.341 | | 380 'caption-free' panels | | ... not a random hold-out
candidates.why_it_matters: The sample sizes and values drift between the two pages and the later one says the sample is not a random hold-out, so neither number is a generalisable accuracy; a planner quoting 38.3% or 56.8% from the audit would cite a figure the next day's page withdrew.

candidates.topic: Where every panel comes from: open-licence published figures only, or also surgical video frames
candidates.statement_a: The card asserts every panel is a figure published under an open licence in a peer-reviewed article or on a public repository.
candidates.quote_a: Every panel is a figure already published under an open licence in a peer-reviewed article or on a public repository; no patient record, DICOM header or institutional image was accessed.
candidates.statement_b: The audit of the same day counts 479 surgical video frames in the corpus, mined from surgical video.
candidates.quote_b: The corpus is eleven thousand panel images mined from the literature and from surgical video. ... surgical video frames | | 479
candidates.why_it_matters: A licence tier or a Dataset B release decided from the card's provenance sentence would include video frames the card says do not exist; the card's statement does not describe the corpus the audit counted.

candidates.topic: Provenance of the corpus versus the closed-journal refetch and the Instagram harvest
candidates.statement_a: The card: every panel is an openly licensed published figure, nothing institutional was accessed.
candidates.quote_a: Every panel is a figure already published under an open licence in a peer-reviewed article or on a public repository; no patient record, DICOM header or institutional image was accessed.
candidates.statement_b: The access setup refetches about 600 closed-journal figures through the owner's institutional sign-in and harvests Instagram with a dedicated account against Meta's terms.
candidates.quote_b: The refetch touches only the closed-journal figures that already carry a matched caption (about 600), one request every three seconds per host ... Meta's terms prohibit automated collection. Accounts used for it get action-blocked, then disabled. Use a dedicated account
candidates.why_it_matters: The overnight report says the proxy session was used on 653 figures; a planner relying on the card would treat the whole corpus as redistributable when part of it came from closed journals and a platform whose terms forbid the collection.

candidates.topic: Rule for sources whose terms forbid automated collection
candidates.statement_a: The access setup plans to harvest Instagram despite Meta's prohibition, by using a dedicated account.
candidates.quote_a: Meta's terms prohibit automated collection. Accounts used for it get action-blocked, then disabled. Use a dedicated account
candidates.statement_b: The registry (2026-10-20) treats the YouTube copies as unpermitted until a request is answered, and the Honest 99 report says Radiopaedia and Eurorad are not scraped.
candidates.quote_b: the YouTube copies are unpermitted until a request is answered
candidates.why_it_matters: The cluster holds two rules at once: harvest around the terms, or hold the copies until permission comes; a planner needs to know which applies before scaling any platform route (the reality check lists scaling YouTube and Instagram under what to stop).

candidates.topic: Releasing FluoroCap (Dataset A and B licence tiers) versus the private-forever rule
candidates.statement_a: The card is a release card with licence tiers, Dataset A and Dataset B, commercial-training eligibility and an examples section.
candidates.quote_a: 10. Examples · Dataset A only (non-commercial or share-alike licences)
candidates.statement_b: The lab recipe (2026-09-27) lists FluoroCap as private forever, never in a public repository or on the website.
candidates.quote_b: Private forever | Level-identification code, FluoroCap, model weights, spinesurg-ct-nnunet, XRSpinoPelvic1K. Never in a public repository, never on the website. | the website shipped 121 MB of weights until 2026-09-14
candidates.why_it_matters: A planner working from the card would prepare a public release the later rule forbids; the card's licence tiers and Dataset A/B split only matter if a release is still intended.

candidates.topic: Whether FluoroCap may train the level model
candidates.statement_a: The audit forbids retraining on the corpus only without re-weighting, so retraining with re-weighting is allowed.

canonical_check.why: The reality check (2026-09-15) re-measures every quantity the audit (2026-09-14) reports, on the refetched corpus of 19,581 images instead of 11,349, and says measurements outrank the morning report; its box rate (17.3% vs 29%), caption-held-out numbers (37.9%/57.1% vs 38.3%/56.8%), modality reading (49% not an x-ray vs detector miss) and Castellvi strata replace the audit's. The audit keeps content the reality check does not repeat (per-level recall, hardware constraints, renderer fixes, the 400-panel read plan), so it is superseded for its numbers, not deleted as a source.

The reality check explicitly supersedes the overnight report's counts (19,048 images, 1,489 refetched, 927 video panels) and says measurements outrank the morning report, so the overnight report is canonical only for what the reality check does not cover; but its 08:30 update postdates the reality check's 06:55 to 07:15 snapshot on the v2 model (registered 08:13, 64.2% on 800 renders) and on the CUT v2 job ids, so on those two items the overnight report is the later record. A superseded relation from overnight-report to reality-check, with the v2 items excepted, fits the records better than two canonical pages.

The card is a frozen 2026-09-14 09:43 view (10,281 rows, dataset 0.2) whose counts, figure-mate number (88%) and provenance sentence are contradicted the same day by the audit and superseded by the reality check (17,486 rows) and the atlas (21,603 rows, 29,500 panels); its licence tiers and release framing conflict with the later private-forever rule. It stays canonical for the licence tiers, inclusion and exclusion rules and the reader protocol, not for counts or release intent.

No later page redraws the pipeline, so the map remains the one description of the routes; its counts (197k frames, manifest v0.3) and its network and serving invariants are dated or contradicted (the access setup's grid plan, the lab recipe's 121 MB of shipped weights, the handoff's anchor_drr leak), so a reader takes its structure and not its numbers.

clusters.unsourced_summary: The dataset card and the pipeline map both assert that the manifest regenerates byte-identical from the same inputs and that an unbroken SHA-256 chain runs from original figure to weights, naming no command, run or checksum file. The map asserts that the grid's outbound IP is captcha-throttled by PMC while WSL is not, and the access setup asserts that publishers authenticate by IP from the university's address space; neither cites a probe, and the overnight report shows the refetch ran through the proxy session instead. The access setup asserts that video frames are the only 1080 px native source and that Instagram serves posts at 1080 px wide, with no measurement; the reality check says the YouTube panels came capped at 720p. The map's anchor panel asserts that an author's printed label is the strongest anchor there is, with no accuracy measured for printed labels, while the reality check says the caption's label was mostly assigned by counting on a limited field. The atlas and the registry both state that 72.8 percent of the 29,500 panels are reproductions with no pixel residual, naming no duplicate-detection run or threshold. The card's 88% figure-mate number carries no pair count. Lift Before Label asserts the renderer is already at the DeepDRR/SyntheX level with no test, and its own adversarial pass never ran. The adjudication bench asserts that the reader's single read is the only ground truth the panel will ever have, and the level verification bench assumes a whole-run-correct panel is the common case; neither assumption is measured, and the card's protocol promises two blind readers with a third adjudicating. The reality check's claims that 'Castellvi I is two thirds of transitional anatomy' and that registration-derived labels are biased are stated without a source in the records.
clusters.stale_summary: All six primary pages are snapshots of 14 to 15 September 2026 with running work inside them: the card says dataset version 0.2 with 0.3 in progress and reader labels pending for every panel; the pipeline map draws manifest v0.3 and 197k YouTube frames; the access setup says the PMC refetch is running now and worries about a library note of 30 June 2026; the overnight report says round two of the refetch is still running, the FluoroGen array was cancelled at 05:50, the CUT v2 is queued as jobs 40285316/7 and the v2 retrain registered at 08:13; the reality check, read between 06:55 and 07:15, says the v2 weights were destroyed and retrain 40285209 is pending, lists CUT jobs 40285274 and 40285275 as queued, and lays out a 90-day and 12-month plan from 15 September. The Honest 99 report of 16 September says training on the enlarged corpus, the backbone comparison and the render-physics test were still running. Later pages date them: the atlas of 2026-10-17 shows human_qc_status pending on all 21,603 rows and the two benches show 0 of 0 verified as of 2026-10-22, so the card's 'reader labels: none yet' still holds five weeks on; the handoff of 2026-10-08 says 14 cine sources, SX-Stitch and Balgrist requests are drafted and none sent, 0 verified real-frame transitional persons against 35 needed, and the registry of 2026-10-20 still calls VinDr's determination pending although the atlas three days earlier says HPR 2026-330 covers it (notice 2026-09-29) and the YouTube copies unpermitted until a request is answered. The lab recipe of 2026-09-27 says the website shipped weights until 2026-09-14. The CNS talk window (31 October to 4 November 2026) and the Radiopaedia USD 250 fee in the records are unconfirmed as of the records' dates.
clusters.notes: Quotes for the primary pages, the Honest 99 report, the handoff, the lab recipe, Lift Before Label, the level context ladder, the OR ledger and the three benches were checked against the plain texts; the extracted texts of fluoroscopy-data-atlas and schwingnet-data-registry truncate their embedded JSON and returned no hits for their key numbers, so those two artifacts are quoted from their inventory records only. One quote named the university's network range, for which an editor's words now stand; no e-mail address, phone number or home address appears, and people are named by role (the owner, the reader). The FluoroGen 12,896 versus synth_rare 12,929 pair may be two different objects; it is listed because no page says so. The overnight report's 08:30 update postdating the reality check's snapshot is why the clustering's two canonical pages disagree on the v2 model state. Several secondary artifacts (Honest 99, handoff, registry, atlas) carry the later word on the corpus and the directive, so a reader of the canonical set alone would miss the private-forever rule, the leaked-family ruling and the October counts.

clusters.unsourced_summary: The cluster asserts a number of things with no source in any record. The clinical-need lines in Naming Vertebrae Without CT and Vertebral Levels Without CT (half of surveyed neurosurgeons report a wrong-level operation; 15 of 100 consecutive discectomies; 179 fiducial placements over 38 months at 52 minutes and 183 mGy) carry no citation in either page. Counting from the Sacrum states that published class-agnostic C-arm detection reaches 0.96 to 0.98 and that the best published registration-free naming is 73.3% importing identity from a preoperative radiograph, with no paper named, and declares the naming problem solved to a standard nobody has published; Ninety-three Pixels says no per-vertebra recall on real fluoroscopy is published and that the 71.67% has no peer, and that LevelCheck's 100% imports identity from the patient's own CT; Research Directions says no lumbosacral 3-D classifier exists at all. The Castellvi type I share (about two thirds in the Honest 99% page, 68% in Research Directions) and the sixth-lumbar prevalence of roughly 2% with a 97%-correct four-lumbar prior (Counting Against Two Anchors) are stated without sources, and the handoff itself says every planning value assumed 95 to 99% that no measurement supports. The handoff and the state-of-the-literature record both say the 97.6% comparator cannot be exceeded at any reachable n, without the calculation, and one calls it a LevelCheck figure and the other a reader figure. The OR-readiness ledger asserts that surgeons centre the field the same way every time and that FluoroCap's article list has no DeepFluoro, C-ArmLSpine, COBRA or Geneva paper, neither shown. The Honest 99% page says every number comes from a named file on the grid but names none, and the overnight report says three independent checks were run without naming them; the lab recipe tallies that 0 of 79 manifest keys begin with a job id. The level bench calls model-decided panels the common case with no count behind it. The REFORMS checklist states the grid's bash 4.2 and Python 3.6 and that a DOI cannot be withdrawn, both unsupported. The LSTV bench's modality and family guesses are machine guesses whose method is not stated.
clusters.stale_summary: As of 2026-10-22 the three benches (SchwingNet/level-verification-bench-mkjxsy, undated; SchwingNet/lstv-verification-bench-6m2qhr, 15 September 2026, pass one; SchwingNet/fluorocap-adjudication-bench-rnsyir, batch b1 from decode_v2_v2.jsonl) all show zero verdicts, and the October 8 records (Research Directions, the state of the literature, the handoff) say the verified real-frame transitional test count is zero. The FluoroCap chain is a sequence of same-week snapshots: the corpus audit (2026-09-14, 11,349 images, no human read), the dataset card (generated 2026-09-14 09:43, v0.1 frozen, v0.3 in progress, reader labels pending for every panel), the overnight report (2026-09-15, updated 08:30, MORNING_REPORT.md to be written, CUT v2 jobs queued), the reality check (2026-09-15 06:55 to 07:35, v2 retrain 40285209 pending, translator jobs queued, reading_set_b1 and reading_v2 built unread, 4,218 empty reader rows, a 90-day and 12-month plan) and the Honest 99% page (2026-09-16, counts against yesterday morning, ordinal-loss arm running, benches awaiting the owner), whose headline the October handoff marks record only. The narrative pages of 2026-09-18 (Naming, Vertebral Levels) have a 376-case CV running, a sacrum detector being built, a tolerant rule in testing and are themselves a post-leak rewrite that the later 92-of-97 audit overtakes. Ninety-three Pixels (2026-09-21) has eight GPU jobs running and a re-render decision left to the owner; the OR-readiness ledger (2026-09-22, re-scored 06:50) has ws_mixed 40411495 running, device fits in progress, the clean DeepFluoro retrain 40411934, a crop re-score pending and the styled corpus queued; Counting from the Sacrum (2026-09-22) has row (d) rendering, an A/B pending on a sampler implemented but not adopted, the fleet detector training on 18,906 frames and the CTSP1K id-is-person audit running, and the handoff says nothing after 2026-09-27 changed the banks. The feasibility study's deep-learning comparator is from October 2025. The lab recipe (2026-09-27) records the public mirror still at v10 and a pelvis DECISION.json never produced; the REFORMS checklist (2026-10-03) says none of its 32 gates exists. The October 8 records leave the dataset-request letters drafted and none sent, CHK-6 and CHK-7 never run, the leak check failing on a stale Geneva fixture, the provisional not recorded as filed against the 30 October deadline, and CNS on 31 October to 4 November 2026. Counting Against Two Anchors is an undated spec whose five arms are not run.
clusters.notes: The clustering gave no superseded or duplicate relations, so canonical_check is empty; the records themselves imply several the clustering omitted: the reality check (2026-09-15) explicitly supersedes the overnight report's image count (19,581 over 19,048); the OR-readiness ledger's 06:50 re-score supersedes its own 06:10 recall figure; Naming Vertebrae Without CT and Vertebral Levels Without CT are two tellings of one 2026-09-18 experiment with shared tables and the same confidentiality line, and the second says an earlier version was superseded after the leak audit; the handoff and Research Directions (2026-10-08) retire the Honest 99% page's headline as record only; Research Directions, the state of the literature and the handoff are one account's one-day audit repeated three times. All quotes are drawn from the inventory records; the plain-text files were not needed. Two number collisions are worth a warning rather than a candidate: 35.7% is both the v1 level model's accuracy on CT renders (audit, reality check) and the coverage at which the Honest 99% page reaches 99%, and 67.4% is both the majority-vote baseline that the sweep lifts to 91.8% and the L6 baseline that 83 real images lift to 73.5%. Several contradictions may be different scoring sets rather than errors (DeepFluoro seed spread, C2 on real, the 8,422-vertebra level-as-class row, count-alone 97.0 vs 99.96), and the why_it_matters says so where the quote does not fix the set. canonical_check.why: The decisions artifact carries the board's decisions, corpus table and licensing sentences forward verbatim and closes the board's open action: the board asks the owner to say go on the IRB-file purge, the decisions artifact records the purge done with git-filter-repo and verified. The decisions artifact also moves numbers the board gives (retraining target ~13,500 to ~34,000, Spinal-AI2024 from do-not-download to revisit), which is what superseding looks like, though the board is dated 2026-09-11 and the decisions artifact is undated.

clusters.unsourced_summary: The cluster asserts a set of field-level claims with no paper, run id or search behind them, and several are copied between artifacts. The board and decisions artifacts both state that no published work uses DRRs to supply level identity to a 2D model and that the published LSTV state of the art is AUC 0.84 at 62.3% prevalence; only research-directions later names the second as Kwak 2025. The field report and the X-ray data handoff both call CSXA the largest annotated lateral set in existence and CM Spine the only public intraoperative source, while other artifacts treat DeepFluoro and C-ArmLSpine as real intraoperative sources. Counting-from-the-sacrum says published class-agnostic C-arm detection reaches 0.96-0.98 and that a 28-point sim-to-real tax matches the field, while ninety-three-pixels says no per-vertebra recall on real fluoroscopy is published and the 71.67% has no peer. The naming note and counting-levels repeat that half of surveyed neurosurgeons report a wrong-level event, 69.6%/97.6% surgeon accuracies, 52 minutes and 183 mGy per event, and 1 in 830 incidence; only the AIDaS proposal and research-directions attach names (Mody 2008, Manbachi 2018, Siminski 2023, Furuya 2026). Counting-against-two-anchors gives a 2% sixth-lumbar prior and a 'documented failure mode' with no document, and the rib audit calls counting from C2 the only definitive method. The decisions artifact gives a ResNet50 source-dataset F1 of 86.6% with no record. The any-view plan's 'lateral naming is at the ceiling' is graded Inferred with no second real device measured, and counting-levels asserts cadaver work needs no IRB while the proposal says the determination covers public de-identified data only.
clusters.stale_summary: The field report (undated, earliest) says the level head is not started, the ignore mask is unused, BUU holds 77 files and CSXA is blocked; the X-ray data handoff's grid state is 'verified 3 Sep 2026' with 800 BUU images never ingested and 0 CSXA on disk. The board (2026-09-11) waits on the owner for the IRB-file purge and is normalising ~22,000 radiographs; the decisions artifact records the purge done, lists Spinal-AI2024 as 'revisit' and a GitHub support ticket open. The ladder (2026-09-13) has jobs 40215523/40215525 running and the VinDr lumbar pipeline in progress; the naming note (2026-09-18) has the 376-patient transitional CV and the Klinwichit training running; counting-from-the-sacrum (2026-09-22) has an A/B and the id-is-a-person audit running and a fleet detector training; the OR ledger (2026-09-22) lists several jobs running, a re-score pending and no device fitted beyond the Cios Fusion; ninety-three-pixels (2026-09-21) has 8 GPU jobs and a decision on the table; what-is-left says the band test is 'being measured right now'. The handoff (2026-10-08) records the disclosure submitted 2026-09-25 with the provisional not recorded, the CNS talk 31 Oct-4 Nov, the Ceph migration and dataset letters not sent; research-directions (2026-10-08) says nothing ran on the grid and letters are not sent. The any-view plan (2026-10-21) has the census job built (PR #76) and going to the grid next, IPCAI 2025 'not yet', and is marked confidential before the provisional and 'before the talk'. The AIDaS proposal (due 2026-10-16, now past) carries [to confirm] placeholders, pending refiner and Fourier arms and a $20,000 request for 2027. The rib audit's v5 is a local tree with nothing pushed and sacral tests next; the two-anchors arms are proposed and not run; the pipeline map's versions are as of its 2026-09-14 commit.
clusters.notes: All 18 records were read whole and every quantity listed was checked against the plain text under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/1b2f17bd-1fd4-5865-b98a-4797cc8ea3ad/scratchpad/text/SchwingNet/. The cluster spans five detector generations (958 images, 4,327, 11,007, 12,709 films, and render-only arms) and several C-ArmLSpine runs (120/141/148/149 cases), and most numeric disagreements are different runs reported as one fact rather than errors; the task was to list them, not to settle them. Items flagged with a caveat: the Ljubljana entries may be two distinct sets; the two patch sizes may belong to two networks; 90% vs 93.9% variance explained may be two quantities. The handoff's 'VinDr-SpineXR (0 of 10,466)' means not in the level bank, not a holding count, and its '2,293 DeepFluoro vendor frames' are the unused vendor frames, distinct from the 366. A file fluorocap-reality-check-czudvb.txt appeared in a grep but is not a member of this cluster and was not used. No e-mail, phone or address was reproduced; people are named by role (the owner, the radiologist, readers).

clusters.cluster: Renders, physics and the sim-to-real gap

candidates.topic: Whether a registered real frame beats its DRR twin as training data (Rapuri 2026 Table 1, DeepFluoro landmarks)
candidates.statement_a: Training on the real frame beats training on its DRR twin: 4.89 vs 7.83 mm; so build the registration route, keep the DRR only as augmentation and fine-tune on real frames.
candidates.quote_a: The DRR at the registered pose is a by-product you get for free, but training on the real frame beats training on that DRR (4.89 vs 7.83 mm landmarks on DeepFluoro, Rapuri 2026 ).
candidates.statement_b: In the same table, DRRs with +/-2.5 degree view augmentation were the best arm at every threshold (4.87 / 6.02 / 9.73), beating real-frame training (4.89) and the generator; physics plus pose augmentation wins everywhere.
candidates.quote_b: DRRs with ±2.5° view augmentation were the best arm at every threshold ( 4.87 / 6.02 / 9.73 ). A generator wins where the detector is already confident and loses where it is not; physics plus pose augmentation wins everywhere.
candidates.why_it_matters: The cluster's answer that registered real frames beat their DRR twins rests on the unaugmented DRR arm only; a planner reading lift-before-label would spend the budget on registering real frames, while what-is-left's reading of the same table says pose-augmented physics DRRs already match or beat them.

candidates.topic: Fraction of a real DeepFluoro frame's variance explained by physics alone (and by the calibrated renderer held out)
candidates.statement_a: Physics alone explains 80.9% of a real frame's attenuation variance (NCC 0.899); a per-frame surface takes the calibrated model to 93.9%.
candidates.quote_a: 80.9% of a real frame's attenuation variance (NCC 0.899), same band shape in every specimen
candidates.statement_b: The stored frames are log-compressed display images; read correctly, physics alone explains 86% rather than 80%, and the calibrated renderer about 90% of a held-out frame.
candidates.quote_b: The stored DeepFluoro frames also turned out to be log-compressed display images; read correctly, physics alone explains 86% of a real frame rather than 80%, and the calibrated renderer about 90% of a held-out one.
candidates.why_it_matters: The 80.9% figure was measured on a mis-read intensity scale; a planner budgeting what a learned term could add would start from the wrong gap (19 points instead of 14) and from an in-sample 93.9% rather than a held-out ~90%.

candidates.topic: Physics-only variance explained and the smooth-field figure quoted in the October proposal and the IRB draft
candidates.statement_a: The renderer explains 80.9% of a real frame's variance, nine device terms add 4.3 points, a per-frame smooth field reaches 93.9% against a 99.5% ceiling (also in the Retrospective Fluoroscopy Protocol).
candidates.quote_a: our renderer explains 80.9% of a real frame's variance; nine calibrated device terms add 4.3 points, held out by specimen; a per-frame smooth field reaches 93.9% against a 99.5% quantum-noise ceiling
candidates.statement_b: Read correctly, physics alone explains 86% and the calibrated renderer about 90% of a held-out frame.
candidates.quote_b: read correctly, physics alone explains 86% of a real frame rather than 80%, and the calibrated renderer about 90% of a held-out one.
candidates.why_it_matters: The grant proposal (October 2026) and the IRB draft carry the pre-correction numbers even though the correction is dated to the 21 September runs; a reviewer or planner would quote 80.9 / 93.9 as current.

candidates.topic: What remains at bone scale after physics and the per-frame field: 'nothing local' versus 2 to 7 times the noise floor
candidates.statement_a: After geometry, physics and nine device terms the residual is a smooth per-frame field with nothing local in it (0.4% of variance at 2 px or finer), so there is nothing for a regional network to learn.
candidates.quote_a: what is left is a smooth per-frame field with nothing local in it — 0.4% of variance at ≤2 px — so there is nothing for a regional network to learn.
candidates.statement_b: After the field the 2 to 16 px bands sit at 0.1 to 0.8% of variance each, two to seven times the noise floor; the 'nothing local' claim was too strong.
candidates.quote_b: After the field, the 2–16 px bands sit at 0.1–0.8% of the frame's variance each — two to seven times the noise floor, not at it.
candidates.why_it_matters: This is the claim the clustering's supersession rests on: ninety-three closes the door on any local learned term, what-is-left reopens it narrowly (bone-edge sharpness) while still advising against a generator.

candidates.topic: What the residual after the calibrated render consists of
candidates.statement_a: The residual edge lines are the real frame being sharper than a 1 mm CT can render, plus bowel gas that moved; the dark right half is collimation and vignette absorbed by the smooth field.
candidates.quote_a: The edge lines are the real frame being sharper than the render: the CT is 1 mm voxels magnified 1.5× onto 0.19 mm pixels, and a render cannot hold detail the CT never had. The bowel mottle is gas that moved between the CT and the fluoroscopy.
candidates.statement_b: Measured by region with the collimator border kept separate, the border ring (a fifth of the field) holds about two thirds of the residual; inside it cortical edges agree to within a few grey levels at every bone thickness; an earlier thin-bone deficit was the border counted as bone and is withdrawn.
candidates.quote_b: the border ring, a fifth of the field, holds about two thirds of the residual, because the real frame falls off through the penumbra and the render stops at a hard edge; inside it, cortical edges agree with the real frame to within a few grey levels at every bone thickness. A thin-bone deficit reported earlier was that border counted as a bone edge, and it has been withdrawn.
candidates.why_it_matters: A planner reading what-is-left would try to add sub-CT sharpness; reading counting-levels would fix the penumbra model at the collimator edge instead. The two pages name different things as the dominant residual.

candidates.statement_a: The CT-to-fluoro map was calibrated, not learned, and transfers because every fitted term belongs to the device.
candidates.quote_a: So it was calibrated , not learned, and it transfers to whole-spine CTs because every fitted term belongs to
candidates.statement_b: Physics-styled frames are not yet statistically inside the real domain (NPS distance 0.111 against a real-vs-real floor of 0.015), so that claim is not made.

candidates.statement_a: The renderer is already at the DeepDRR/SyntheX level; only its randomisation list needs checking.

candidates.statement_b: A saturating clip on 8 to 11 correlated terms meant the device-card renders reached only 1.7 to 5.1% of the fitted joint distribution, with 94.9 to 98.3% of frames carrying a pinned term; the replacement sampler is not adopted.

canonical_check.why: What Is Left After Physics explicitly revises ninety-three's residual claim ('nothing local' was too strong; the 2-16 px bands sit at two to seven times the noise floor) and keeps the same calibrated renderer, so for the residual decomposition the supersession holds. It is partial: what-is-left is undated and carries none of ninety-three's other content (the 836-to-139 px downsampling ladder, the +4.3/+4.1 device-term gain, scatter width 15.8 px, the 597-frame detector and its 76.9% and 26-point spread, the C2 finding, the re-render decision), and Counting Levels Under Fluoroscopy (runs of 21 September) supersedes both on the variance figures (86% physics, ~90% held-out, border ring holds two thirds of the residual, thin-bone deficit withdrawn). A planner should read ninety-three for calibration and resolution, what-is-left for the residual, and counting-levels for the corrected numbers.

clusters.unsourced_summary: The cluster asserts several things with no source or measurement in any page. The comparators for the project's own numbers are the weakest: Counting From The Sacrum gives 'the best published registration-free naming is 73.3%' and 'published class-agnostic C-arm detection reaches 0.96-0.98' with no citation, and says the 28-point sim-to-real tax 'matches what the field reports' without naming the field; Ninety-Three Pixels says the opposite ('no per-vertebra recall on real fluoroscopy is published at all') also without a search record on the page. Both Ninety-Three Pixels and Counting From The Sacrum state that LevelCheck's 100% imports identity from the patient's own CT by registration without citing it (Lift Before Label, Any-View Spine Plan and the Reality Check do cite Lo 2015 and De Silva 2016). The AIDaS proposal and the Retrospective Fluoroscopy Protocol share the inference that 'synthetic fluoroscopy from CT is close in physics but tuned to one C-arm and one cadaveric population', drawn from DeepFluoro alone before any second device was fitted. Lift Before Label asserts that the renderer 'is already at the DeepDRR/SyntheX level', that 'the OR always has both' AP and lateral views, that registration-derived labels are biased toward registration-friendly frames, and that the level's discriminating cues are projected rather than depth-ambiguous features; none is measured anywhere in the cluster, and the first is contradicted by the sampler audit and the ledger's styling distances. Ninety-Three Pixels asserts that 'vertebral bodies are large, low-frequency objects and the detector does not need the pixels' as the reading of a flat ladder, which the Level Context Ladder's 48-to-96 px gain and the Reality Check's 2.6x sharpness gap qualify for naming. Any-View says 'renders add unlimited exact pairs' and Lift says the registered DRR 'is a by-product you get for free'; neither costs rendering or registration. What Is Left After Physics asserts that bowel gas 'is not a function of the CT' and that 'YOLO11 is BatchNorm' without reference. The OR Readiness Ledger asserts that 'surgeons centre the field the same way every time' and that 'the crops are upscaled windows, so a detector ... loses most of them' as explanations rather than measurements. The data registry's 'only' claims (the only confirmed lumbar cine, the only large real thoracic fluoroscopy without a DUA, the only voxel-anchored C1/C2/C7 source) and the Reality Check's unverified device-frame figures (OEC, Ziehm native frame sizes) are search summaries, not verified facts.
clusters.stale_summary: Every primary page is a dated snapshot with open work. Ninety-Three Pixels (21 Sep 2026, 03:3x EDT) has eight GPU arms live, dr_eval queued, DeepFluoro 'acquired, not yet inspected', two manuscript word counts (6,299 and 7,244) and the re-render decision left to the owner; Any-View Spine Plan (21 Oct) shows the renderer question still open (ablation #69). What Is Left After Physics (undated, 2026) says recall holds are 'being measured directly right now' and three direct tests 'are next', one of which (the Fourier low-band swap) Counting Levels Under Fluoroscopy already reports from the 21 September runs. Lift Before Label (15 Sep) never ran its verification pass ('scheduled to run when the limit resets'), lists the registration harness as running and Protocol 1's frames as 'still to come'; the Retrospective Fluoroscopy Protocol is still 'Date Submitted: Draft' with a January 2027 target and dozens of [to confirm] fields, and the AIDaS proposal's 16 October 2026 deadline has passed with the PI slot unfilled and refiner results 'pending'. The OR Readiness Ledger (22 Sep 06:10, re-scored 06:50) has the clean DeepFluoro retrain (job 40411934), crop re-scores, device fits (jobs 40411903-07, 40412003, 40412010), the SpineSAC inventory, the device census and the multi-device corpus chain (renders 40411951/53/55, trainings 40411961-66) all running or queued, 'no styled corpus exists', and the whole-spine curves still on the 312-box denominator. Counting From The Sacrum (22 Sep) has the fleet-wide detector training (18,906 frames), the sampler A/B running, the CTSpinoPelvic1K id audit running and figure row (d) rendering; SchwingNet Figures (22 Sep 22:50) has Figures 3, 4 and 6 and Table 1 being fixed and the integration pass running. The FluoroCap pages are a 14-15 September snapshot: the Pipeline Map's FluoroGen loop was dropped the next morning, the Overnight Report's refetch round two, v2 retrain (registered 08:13), CUT v2 (jobs 40285316/7) and Instagram/YouTube harvests were running, and the Reality Check's v2 retrain (40285209) and translator (40285274/5) were pending with human_qc_status 'pending' on all 17,486 manifest rows; by 20 October the Data Registry rules FluoroCap out of training (directive D1). The Level Context Ladder (13 Sep 11:30) has the +BUU rungs and VinDr pseudo-labelling relaunched (jobs 40215523, 40215525); the Vertebra Detector Field Report is undated with the level head 'not started' and the ignore mask 'not yet in this run', both overtaken. The Data Registry (20 Oct) lists fourteen video-source requests drafted in September and never sent, COBRA Varian geometry solved 23 September with no bank built, 175 COBRA cases embargoed to 2032-03-01, VinDr's IRB determination pending, the BUU licence unread, case39 unexported, LUMOS never fetched and RSNA 2022 never unpacked; Any-View (21 Oct) has the census (PR #76) about to go to the grid, IPCAI 2025 'not yet', and everything confidential before the provisional (by 30 October) and the talk of 2 November 2026.
clusters.notes: Records and texts were read whole for all three primary members and all fourteen secondary members; plain texts were consulted for the ledger's device-card table, ninety-three's GAN and residual sentences, counting-levels' log-compression and border-ring correction, what-is-left's Rapuri reading, lift's LevelCheck and Pelphix lines, any-view's detection table and the reality check's corrected literature figures. Two cautions for the planner: the clustering's canonical choice of Lift Before Label rests on a page whose verification pass never ran and whose Jecklin, Spine-DART and Pelphix numbers the same-day Reality Check corrected; and the cluster's answer 'registered real frames beat their DRR twins' is one reading of Rapuri 2026 Table 1 (real 4.89 vs unaugmented DRR 7.83) while What Is Left After Physics reads the same table as pose-augmented DRRs (4.87) matching or beating real frames at every threshold. The numbers most often re-quoted downstream (80.9% physics, 93.9% smooth field, 96-98% population-matched sacrum, +4.3 device terms, 76.9% pooled sacrum) each have a later correction in the cluster (86% and ~90% held-out in Counting Levels; 88.5-91.3% clean and 64.0% v2 in the Ledger; +1.3 on the device card) that the October grant and IRB pages do not carry. Candidates about dataset counts (C-ArmLSpine 141/148/149 cases, TotalSegmentator 156/142 whole spines, CTSpinoPelvic1K 801/802, FluoroCap 19,048/19,581/29,484/29,500 panels) are included because the render and test arms are sized from them. No e-mail address, phone number or home address is reproduced; people are named by role.

canonical_check.why: Both are WSU eProtocol drafts of 'Protocol 1' for the retrospective fluoroscopy collection, mirroring IRB-21-10-4123. The retrospective protocol is the later text: it cites the 2 September 2026 determination 2026_269, the 16 October 2026 AIDaS deadline and a January 2027 start, where the other is dated 15 September 2026 and says 'Unfunded / departmental'. Neither record could confirm the order from its own text, but the dates and the AIDaS grant's 'builds-on' relation settle it. Caveat: the later draft is a redesign rather than a revision: Expedited 5 instead of Exempt 4, one surgeon's 2021-2026 cases instead of 40,000 studies from 2006, detector recall from operative-note truth instead of CT-registered labels, and the fracture-detection and registry-linkage aims, the 6,000-vertebrae stratified target and the 'Protocol 2 submitted alongside' line are dropped, not carried. The two also come from different accounts. So 'superseded' holds for the submission, but the older draft's aims are abandoned, and downstream notes (lift-before-label) still expect its registered frames.

clusters.unsourced_summary: The cluster's business case is held up by figures no artifact sources. The proposal (counting-levels-under-fluoroscopy), the seed grant (aidas-seed-grant-proposal) and the protocol (retrospective-fluoroscopy-protocol) all say every radiation-safety prerequisite takes fifteen business days, with no WSU page cited. The proposal and the grant assume the DMC PACS holds every saved fluoroscopic series of one surgeon's spine cases for 2021-2026 with operative notes and post-operative imaging for truth, while the older eProtocol draft and the fluorocap note cite another centre where half the cases were off PACS and the protocol's frames-per-case waits on a 20-case pilot. The proposal says cadaver work needs no IRB, the grant leaves phantom IACUC/RSC open, and the cadaver fee ($1,000-3,000) and the GPU, Jetson, grabber and phantom prices are list estimates with no quotes. The ten operating-room minutes saved per case (proposal) rest on two small non-randomised thoracic series that the visual abstract itself calls the weakest input, inflated by an unexplained 1.35 to 2026 dollars. The navigation comparison in the abstract, the grant and the protocol states that no study shows navigation reduces wrong-level surgery and that no verified capital cost exists, and the abstract's $1.5M over seven years plus 10% service is declared an assumption. Joint Commission 2024 (127, 9, 7, 36%) and NHS England (185) are cited by organisation name only in the grant, the protocol and the abstract; the proposal's registry figures carry no inline citation at all. The protocol's reason for Expedited 5, that research supporting an FDA submission cannot be exempt, and its line that the WSU form limits review to Exempt 2 and 3, cite no regulation; its sentence that synthetic fluoroscopy is tuned to one C-arm and one population is an inference from DeepFluoro alone; its expectation that a full count is possible on only a minority of archived cases is marked to confirm. The older draft's statements that no public intraoperative fluoroscopy with level labels exists (contradicted by the atlas) and that most spine-surgery patients have a pre- or post-operative CT have no source. Among the secondary notes, vertebral-levels-without-ct gives every literature figure without a citation and says 'fixing it took naming from 67% to 92%' with no run named, counting-from-the-sacrum says the 28-point sim-to-real tax 'matches what the field reports elsewhere almost exactly' without the field's numbers, and the OR-readiness ledger's 97% counting-grade threshold is a chosen line, not a derived one.
clusters.stale_summary: The proposal (counting-levels-under-fluoroscopy, September 2026) says 'Start this week' on the WSU C-arm and takes every synthetic number from the runs of 21 September 2026; on 21 October the grid-pipeline note records zero grid jobs run, gate words under review in PR #54 and one press by the owner outstanding, with a schedule of first shards 23 Oct, version 1 trained 28 Oct, latency 29 Oct, provisional filed 30 Oct and the CNS mini-oral 2 Nov, and the RSNA RATIC link expiring 2026-10-28. The seed grant (aidas-seed-grant-proposal) was due October 16, 2026, now past, with the submission address, PI, case count and the $24/h rate still '[to confirm]', biosketches undrafted, refiner results 'pending' that the proposal already tabled, and a manuscript 'in preparation' that the 8 October handoff says is held pending the technology-transfer office, with the disclosure filed 2026-09-25 and no provisional recorded. The retrospective protocol is 'Date Submitted: Draft', expects AIDaS notification December 16, 2026 and a January 2027 start, and leaves frames per case and the verification fraction to a 20-case pilot; the older eProtocol draft of 15 September 2026 carries '40,000 studies — unconfirmed', '7 years — confirm', citations to insert and a pending trauma co-investigator. Neither protocol nor the grant mentions the HPR 2026-330 supplement of 29 September that the atlas records, and the atlas (17 October) still asks whether DUA data needs its own determination. The atlas lists eleven unsent Outlook drafts and an unconfirmed USD 250 Radiopaedia fee; the grid note says the Radiopaedia licence waits on countersignature and JHU had not replied on 21 October; the handoff of 8 October had the cine-source letters 'drafted; none sent'. The research-directions note (8 October) counts zero verified transitional real-frame test persons against 35 needed, while vertebral-levels-without-ct (18 September) had a 376-patient transitional cross-validation 'running now'; counting-from-the-sacrum and what-is-left-after-physics (22 September) describe training and measurements in progress whose results no cluster artifact reports. The lab recipe notes the public mirror still at v10 on 2026-09-27 and weights shipped on the website until 2026-09-14. The outreach note read funder pages in September 2026 and expects RSNA cycles to open in October. The lift-before-label note's verification pass never ran and it still expects registered frames from the older Protocol 1 design; the fluorocap note has the PACS capture object type undetermined and FluoroCap QC pending on all 21,603 rows.
clusters.notes: All nineteen records were read in full except SchwingNet__fluorocap-reality-check-czudvb.json, read to line 1053 of 1290 (the unread tail is the end of external_sources and the trailing metadata). Quotes are taken from the records' quote fields; the artifacts' plain text under scratchpad/text/SchwingNet/ was not consulted. Two quotes are paraphrases of record decision fields rather than page text: the grant's 'not eligible to serve as PI' and the older draft's 'a first-year surgery resident at DMC'. Items noted but not listed as candidates: the atlas's own open question of 13 versus 6 Balgrist specimens (letter versus paper) sits inside one artifact; the CNS dates '2 Nov, mini-oral 66629' and '31 Oct to 4 Nov 2026' are a day and a meeting range, not a conflict; Manbachi 2018 is quoted as 30.4%/2.4% error in two notes and 69.6%/97.6% correct in another, which agree; LSTV prevalence appears as 15.3% (83 studies), 12.9% of lumbar surgical patients, 15-25%, and 9-11% count-changing types II-IV, which are different quantities but will confuse a stratum definition; the registration-free feasibility note (15 September) says no surviving claim gives wrong-level incidence, which the later documents take from Furuya 2026 rather than from that verified set. The detector field report says none of its tests are cross-site and recall is not reported globally by design, while the proposal, grant and protocol quote 99.14% per-body recall; whether that is the same detector is not established by the records. People are named by role throughout; no contact details appear in the records' quotes used here.

clusters.cluster: Symphony: the protocol, its evidence and its place

canonical_check.why: The clustering lists no superseded or duplicate relation to bear out. The brief (2026-10-14) is the one artifact that tallies the seventeen guarantees and names which lane checks each; it is canonical for that, though its numbers (59 mutants, depth 5, F8 open, deep lane unmerged) are the oldest in the cluster and the spec and competitors note carry the later ones.

Dated 2026-10-16, it is the latest word on the validation numbers (twelve fixes on main, 109 mutants, #35 merged, the guard's directory bug) and the only one that withdraws the 8-pair coordbench figures; it overlaps the spec heavily on CooperBench and prior art and should be read for the 'what not to claim' list.

The spec is the source the manual, the competitors note and the brief cite by section; it alone grades each claim (Verified, Inferred, Reported, Open) and lists the risks and research questions. Its one weakness is that it reports the 8-pair pass counts that the competitors note later calls not reportable.

It is the reader's guide to the spec and adds the verification passes (verify/02's three findings, the adversarial search of 25 systems) that the spec summarises; it duplicates the spec's figures rather than superseding them, so it is canonical as the method record, not as a number source.

The handoff (2026-10-13) is the only record of the decisions of that night (the pool, the runtime, the QA gate, spine-program's state, the measured dropped cron slots, the plan ladder's unconfirmed $4 prices) and says itself its state lines were not rechecked against GitHub; it is canonical for decisions and dated state, not for numbers the later three artifacts moved. The ladder (2026-10-09), left non-canonical, is nonetheless the cluster's only pricing source with a verification date and should be read beside it.

clusters.unsourced_summary: The cluster asserts several load-bearing claims with no source opened. The taxonomy spec (SchwingNet/symphony-and-beethoven-taxonomy-spec-lcbqro) and the competitors note (symphony-template/symphony-versus-competitors-lynwzk) both carry Cursor's report that naive locks collapsed 20 agents to the throughput of two or three and a 2026 noise-floor study putting single-seed gains under about 15 points inside noise; both are graded Reported and unnamed, the competitors note says no primary source was opened for either, and the brief (symphony-template/symphony-in-brief-9cdciz) says its Cursor row is from memory because cursor.com is blocked. The spec's argument that GitHub's free public minutes are alone in the market rests on four withdrawal dates (Travis 2020, GitLab 2021, Azure DevOps 2026 and 2027, Cirrus 2026-06-01) of which it verifies two and the manual (symphony-template/symphony-and-beethoven-taxonomy-manual-re4jtx) still asks a pass to confirm, plus a CircleCI credit cap 'Reported, from its pricing page by search'. The spec appends 'Self-hosted runners are free on every plan' to a cited quote without a citation of its own, and its risk 3 (the account reached its weekly limit on 2026-10-15) and risk 9 (Wayne State's approval, no BAA on a personal plan, Remote Control under HIPAA) link no record. The atomic claim on github.com is stated as fact by the shared plan (symphony-template/shared-multi-account-claude-project-plan-rqzwh9), the build plan (symphony-template/sdlc-build-plan-bjzikn) and the brief while the spec's R4 leaves it open, the canary's C7 runs by hand and the manual's verify/02 ran on a scratch repository. 'Branch protection on a private repository needs a paid plan' is sourced to a docs page in the shared plan, marked 'to be checked, not assumed' in the build plan and attributed to 'document 25' in the primitives spec (symphony-template/sdlc-primitives-spec-ldx4zd), and no artifact records the check. The grid review (symphony-template/grid-and-cloud-claude-workers-review) and the handoff (symphony-template/symphony-handoff) use a 90-minute cloud-worker limit, a seven-day window for remote-control --continue and 'six 90-minute runs' per schedule without saying where they were read; the shared plan's 'hooks are not loaded in a Project with several repos' and its February 2026 ban reports (a blog's guess, unconfirmed by Anthropic) are likewise untested here. The ladder (symphony-template/the-dollar-per-feature-ladder-9ymg61) alone gives Windows 1.7x and macOS 10x runner multipliers and 'about a minute per pull request event', the figure its whole monthly-minute arithmetic rests on. The handoff could not confirm the GitHub Pro and Team $4 prices the ladder says it verified, and its 'enterprise OpenGrid' name has no source.

Its steps 7 and 8 (secrets in claude-swap-cloud, the in-repository release-kit script) are superseded by the handoff's symphony-extension location and the shared chrome-store-release-kit, and the Beethoven runbook of 2026-10-13 is the later description of the same automatic release path; the PyPI publish and the submission it waits on are not recorded as done anywhere in the cluster.

clusters.unsourced_summary: The cluster's load-bearing product facts are mostly sourced once and then repeated as settled. "A Project belongs to one user" is quoted from the Claude Code documentation only in the plan of 2026-10-08 (shared-multi-account-claude-project-plan); the primitives spec attributes it to an unshown "document 25", and the build plan and the student onboarding state it bare. "Branch protection on a private repository needs a paid plan" is linked to GitHub's page in the plan, then carried by the spec (via document 25 and move-gaps.md), the build plan (which says it is to be checked), the ladder and the store runbook, while the handoff later infers the organization is on Enterprise Cloud without reading a settings page. The routine caps (30 fires an hour per routine, 100 per account) rest on the plan's one link and are restated as "runs" by the build plan. The Consumer Terms are paraphrased in the plan, the spec, the build plan and the Slurm playbook with no quoted clause; the playbook's "pooling tokens is what the terms prohibit" and the plan's "grey zone" both lack a citation beyond a third-party ban report the plan itself marks unconfirmed, and the handoff's account-pool decision rests on the owner's word. Both Chrome Web Store runbooks assert Google OAuth lifetimes (refresh tokens from a Testing consent screen die after seven days; an unused client or token after six months), review times ("several days" against "one to three days"), that a lower version is refused, that Public can follow Unlisted without a new review, and that release runs never overlap, none with a page cited. The store runbook's Windows-double and macOS-tenfold multipliers and the ladder's 1.7x and 10x are both uncited at the sentence.
